full_record.title: Mutual-visibility conjecture for distance-hereditary graphs
full_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a distance-hereditary graph. A **big-$\mu$ cograph without universal vertices** is a cograph of the form $G=(K_1\cup K_t)+H$ without universal vertices, as described in the preceding characterization. **Mutual-visibility conjecture.** If $G$ is a distance-hereditary graph but not a big-$\mu$ cograph without universal vertices, then

$$
\mu(G)=\mu_{\rm t}(G).
$$

This conjecture seeks to characterize the distance-hereditary graphs for which the mutual-visibility number exceeds the total mutual-visibility number, extending the established classification for cographs. The supplied text gives no resolution status beyond the conjectural formulation.
full_record.source_name: Serafino Cicerone, Gabriele Di Stefano, Sandi Klavžar and Ismael G. Yero, “Mutual-visibility problems on graphs of diameter two”, arXiv:2401.02373 (2024).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02373

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

full_record.title: Domination bound for complementary self-centered graphs
full_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$. Write $\overline{G}$ for its complement, and let $\gamma(G)$ denote the domination number of $G$. A graph is in $SCC(2)$ when both $G$ and $\overline{G}$ are self-centered and

$$
\operatorname{rad}(G)=\operatorname{diam}(G)=\operatorname{rad}(\overline{G})=\operatorname{diam}(\overline{G})=2.
$$

**Domination conjecture for $SCC(2)$ graphs.** If $G\in SCC(2)$, then

$$
\gamma(G)\leq\left\lceil\sqrt{n}\right\rceil
$$

and

$$
\gamma(\overline{G})\leq\left\lceil\sqrt{n}\right\rceil.
$$

The paper introduces this conjecture for the exceptional class left after proving polynomial-time decidability outside $SCC(2)$. It would give simultaneous domination-number bounds for a graph and its complement in the unresolved case.
full_record.source_name: Subramanian Arumugam, Suresh Manjanath Hegde and Shashanka Kulamarva, “An improved upper bound for the domination number of a graph”, arXiv:2401.02765 (2024).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02765

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

full_record.title: Weak minimality conjecture for the chromatic algebra generating set
full_record.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}_n$ be the $n$th-order chromatic algebra and let $E_n$ be the generating set appearing in the paper. **Weak minimality conjecture.** The set $E_n$ is a minimal generating set in the weak sense: no proper subset of $E_n$ generates $\mathcal{C}_n$. The preceding theorem establishes that $E_n$ generates $\mathcal{C}_n$; the conjecture asserts that every element of $E_n$ is necessary, while minimality was not proved in the source.
full_record.source_name: Ethan Yi-Heng Liu, “On the Structure and Generators of the nth-order Chromatic Algebra”, arXiv:2401.06095 (2024).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.06095

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

full_record.title: Nasr's monotonicity conjecture for Kazhdan–Lusztig and $Z$-polynomials
full_record.statement:
Let $M$ and $M'$ be matroids, and let $\varphi:M\to M'$ be a morphism in the category $\mathcal{M}$. Let $P_M(t)$ and $P_{M'}(t)$ denote their Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials, and let $Z_M(t)$ and $Z_{M'}(t)$ denote their $Z$-polynomials. **Nasr's monotonicity conjecture.** For any morphism $\varphi:M\to M'$ in $\mathcal{M}$, the polynomials

$$
P_M(t)-P_{M'}(t)\qquad\text{and}\qquad Z_M(t)-Z_{M'}(t)
$$

have non-negative coefficients. This conjecture extends an unpublished conjecture of Gedeon for uniform matroids and predicts that these valuative invariants are monotone under matroid morphisms, as is known for the Chow and augmented Chow polynomials.
full_record.source_name: Ben Elias, Dane Miyata, Nicholas Proudfoot and Lorenzo Vecchi, “Categorical valuative invariants of polyhedra and matroids”, arXiv:2401.06869 (2024).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.06869

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

full_record.title: Endpoint-1 conjecture for weakly consecutive sequences
full_record.statement: Let $\sigma$ be a weakly consecutive sequence, meaning a permutation of $\{1,\ldots,k\}$ such that if $d$ divides $\sigma(i)$, then $d$ also divides $\sigma(i\pm d)$ wherever these terms are defined. **Endpoint-1 conjecture.** Any WCS either begins or ends with the term $1$; equivalently, $\sigma(1)=1$ or $\sigma(k)=1$. The authors have not proved this directly from the definition, so the claim remains open.
full_record.source_name: Thomas Garrison, Chris Seiler and Andrew Knowles, “Weakly Consecutive Sequences”, arXiv:2401.09497 (2024).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.09497

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

full_record.title: Boundary-location conjecture for small entries in weakly consecutive sequences
full_record.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a weakly consecutive sequence, and let $m<k/2$. **Boundary-location conjecture.** Each $m$ appears among either the first $m$ or the last $m$ terms of the sequence; equivalently, its position satisfies

$$
\sigma^{-1}(m)\in[1,m]\cup[k-m+1,k].
$$

The paper presents this as a consequence of the endpoint-1 conjecture together with an earlier lemma, but it is itself stated as a conjecture and remains open.
full_record.source_name: Thomas Garrison, Chris Seiler and Andrew Knowles, “Weakly Consecutive Sequences”, arXiv:2401.09497 (2024).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.09497

full_record.title: The minimiser conjecture for doubling in compact Lie groups
full_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected Lie group, let $H$ be a proper closed subgroup of maximal dimension, and for $\delta>0$ define its $\delta$-neighbourhood by

$$
H_{\delta}:=\{g\in G:d(g,H)<\delta\}.
$$

For a measurable subset $A\subset G$, its doubling constant is $\mu_G(A^2)/\mu_G(A)$.

**Doubling minimiser conjecture.** The subset $H_{\delta}$ minimises the doubling constant among measurable subsets $A$ satisfying

$$
\mu_G(A)=\mu_G(H_{\delta}).
$$

The conjecture concerns the precise minimisers underlying the sharp small-set doubling bounds. The source presents it as a conjecture and does not state a resolution.
full_record.source_name: Simon Machado, “Minimal doubling for small subsets in compact Lie groups”, arXiv:2401.14062 (2024).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.14062

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2024). “They proved in the conjecture for sets of at least exponential size.”

full_record.title: Brändén–D’León relaxation conjecture for the weak half-plane property
full_record.statement: A **matroid has the weak half-plane property** when its set of bases agrees with the support of a stable polynomial. A **relaxation** of a matroid is obtained by relaxing a circuit-hyperplane. **Brändén–D’León's conjecture.** If a matroid $M$ has the weak half-plane property, then every relaxation of $M$ also has the weak half-plane property. The paper gives a relaxation of the matroid $P_8$ that does not have the weak half-plane property, disproving the conjecture.
full_record.source_name: Mario Kummer and David Sawall, “Three results related to the half-plane property of matroids”, arXiv:2402.01272 (2024).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01272

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of February 2024); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

full_record.title: The acyclic digraph cellular–singular cubical homology conjecture
full_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a digraph. Write $H_*^{\operatorname{cell}}(G;\mathbb R)$ for its cellular homology and $H_*^c(G;\mathbb R)$ for its singular cubical homology. **The cellular–singular cubical homology conjecture.** If $G$ is acyclic, then

$$
H_*^{\operatorname{cell}}(G;\mathbb R)\cong H_*^c(G;\mathbb R).
$$

In particular, the admissible relations among the admissible pairs are the boundary conditions in the singular cubical homology. The conjecture identifies the cellular chain construction with the singular cubical theory for acyclic digraphs; the paper motivates it through the relation between these complexes but does not state a resolution.
full_record.source_name: Xinxing Tang and Shing-Tung Yau, “The Cellular Homology of Digraphs”, arXiv:2402.05682 (2025).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.05682

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

full_record.title: Polytopality conjecture for hyperbolic posets
full_record.statement: Let $F$ be a real-rooted polynomial and let $\mathcal{H}_s(F)$ be its hyperbolic slice, stratified by root multiplicity compositions; the associated hyperbolic poset records the incidence relations among these strata. **Polytopality conjecture.** Hyperbolic posets are polytopal, meaning that each hyperbolic poset is isomorphic to the face lattice of a polytope. The examples suggest this because the strata have geometric and combinatorial properties reminiscent of polytopes, although the strata themselves need not be convex; the paper leaves the question open.
full_record.source_name: Arne Lien and Robin Schabert, “Shellable slices of hyperbolic polynomials and the degree principle”, arXiv:2402.05702 (2024).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.05702

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

full_record.title: Choe–Oxley–Sokal–Wagner's rank-three transversal matroid conjecture
full_record.statement:
A **transversal matroid** is a matroid obtained from a family of subsets by declaring a set independent when it can be matched injectively to distinct members of the family. A matroid has the **half-plane property** when its basis generating polynomial is nonvanishing whenever all variables lie in a common open half-plane.

**Rank-three transversal matroid conjecture.** Every transversal matroid of rank $3$ has the half-plane property.

The conjecture was first posed in the cited earlier work and is described by the source as still open. It is directly related to the paper's investigation of half-plane properties for classes of transversal matroids.
full_record.source_name: Ayush Kumar Tewari, “Transversal matroids and the half plane property”, arXiv:2402.06302 (2024).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06302

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

full_record.title: The $K_{2,d}$-free path conjecture for tree-independence number
full_record.statement: For positive integers $d$ and $s$, a graph is **$\{K_{2,d},P_s\}$-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{2,d}$ or the $s$-vertex path $P_s$. **The $K_{2,d}$-and-path conjecture.** For any two positive integers $d$ and $s$, the class of $\{K_{2,d},P_s\}$-free graphs has bounded tree-independence number. This is posed as a weakening of the previously stated biclique-and-path conjecture; the source presents it as an open direction.
full_record.source_name: Clément Dallard, Matjaž Krnc, O-joung Kwon, Martin Milanič, Andrea Munaro, Kenny Štorgel and Sebastian Wiederrecht, “Treewidth versus clique number. IV. Tree-independence number of graphs excluding an induced star”, arXiv:2402.11222 (2024).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.11222

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2024). “While the conjecture is still open, the following partial results are known.”

full_record.title: Cho et al.'s spectral conjecture for [a,b]-factors
full_record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and let $b\ge a$ be two positive integers such that $na\equiv 0\pmod{2}$ and $n\ge a+1$. Here, $\lambda(G)$ denotes the spectral radius of $G$, $K_{a-1}\lor(K_1\cup K_{n-a})$ is the join of $K_{a-1}$ with the disjoint union of $K_1$ and $K_{n-a}$, and an **$[a,b]$-factor** is a spanning subgraph whose vertex degrees lie between $a$ and $b$. **Cho et al.'s spectral conjecture.** If

$$
\lambda(G)>\lambda\bigl(K_{a-1}\lor(K_1\cup K_{n-a})\bigr),
$$

then $G$ contains an $[a,b]$-factor.
This conjecture proposes a spectral-radius sufficient condition for the existence of an $[a,b]$-factor. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
full_record.source_name: Zengzhao Xu, Ligong Wang and Weige Xi, “Spectral extremal problems for (a,b,k)-critical and fractional (a,b,k)-critical graphs”, arXiv:2512.20971 (2025).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.20971

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

full_record.title: Brešar–Togni conjecture on packing coloring of subdivided subcubic graphs
full_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph in which every vertex has degree at most $3$, and let $S(G)$ be the graph obtained by subdividing every edge of $G$, replacing each edge $uv$ by a path $u$-$w$-$v$ through a new vertex $w$. **Brešar–Togni conjecture.** Every subcubic graph satisfies

$$
\chi_p(S(G))\leq 5.
$$

This conjecture asks for a universal upper bound on the packing chromatic number of the subdivision of a subcubic graph. It arose from work of Gastineau and Togni and was subsequently formalized by Brešar et al.; its resolution is not specified in the source.
full_record.source_name: Xin Zhang and Dezhi Zou, “Fast algorithm for S-packing coloring of Halin graphs”, arXiv:2512.22809 (2025).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.22809

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

full_record.title: The $3k-4$ conjecture for subsets of $\mathbb F_p$
full_record.statement:
Let $p$ be a large prime number and let $A
e\varnothing$ be a subset of $\mathbb F_p$. An additive set $A$ has the **covering property** if it can be covered by an arithmetic progression of length $|2A|-|A|+1$.

**$3k-4$ conjecture.** If

$$
|A+A|\le \min\{3|A|-4,p-1\},
$$

then $A$ has the covering property.

The conjecture is the analogue over $\mathbb F_p$ of Freiman's $3k-4$ theorem for finite subsets of the integers. It remains open, despite progress under additional assumptions on the extension ratio or density.
full_record.source_name: Xin Wei, Xiande Zhang and Gennian Ge, “The Hilton-Milner type results of (k, )-sum-free sets in F_p^n”, arXiv:2512.22835 (2025).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.22835

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2025). “Although many efforts have been taken during the decades , the $3k-4$ conjecture is still open.”

full_record.title: Godsil's edge-connectivity conjecture for colour classes in association schemes
full_record.statement:
Let an **association scheme** be a finite set equipped with relations whose colour classes are the graphs arising from the corresponding adjacency matrices. For a graph $G$, let $\lambda(G)$ denote its edge-connectivity, and let its degree mean its regular vertex degree.

**Godsil's conjecture.** If $G$ is a connected graph which is a colour class in an association scheme, then

$$
\lambda(G)=\text{degree of }G.
$$

The conjecture is solved in the source: the authors prove that every connected regular equiarboreal graph has edge-connectivity equal to its degree, and colour classes in association schemes are equiarboreal and regular.
full_record.source_name: Wensheng Sun, Yujun Yang and Shou-Jun Xu, “A solution to Godsil's conjecture on the edge-connectivity of graphs in association schemes”, arXiv:2512.22977 (2025).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.22977

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2025). “Brouwer's conjecture has been proved by Brouwer and Koolen for distance-regular graphs, but remains an open problem in the other cases.”

full_record.title: Conjecture on universal polar dual pairs of spherical codes
full_record.statement: Let $C$ be a PULB-optimal code, and let $D$ be its set of universal minima. Assume that $D$ is in general position, meaning that $D$ is not contained in a hyperplane. **Universal polar dual pair conjecture.** The code $C$ together with $D$ forms a PULB-optimal pair $(C,D)$ and generates a maximal PULB-optimal pair, and hence a universal polar dual pair. This conjecture is motivated by the fact that all examples of PULB-optimal configurations found so far satisfy the asserted property; its general validity remains open.
full_record.source_name: S. V. Borodachov, P. G. Boyvalenkov, P. D. Dragnev, D. P. Hardin, E. B. Saff and M. M. Stoyanova, “Universal polar dual pairs of spherical codes found in E_8 and Λ_24”, arXiv:2512.25037 (2025).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.25037

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

full_record.title: Dependent internal tree-ordering expansions and bounded twin-width
full_record.statement: Let $\mathscr C$ be a hereditary weakly sparse class of graphs. An **internal tree-ordering expansion** of a graph is an expansion by the forest-ordering defined by a spanning forest; $\mathscr C$ has a dependent internal tree-ordering expansion when such expansions form a monadically dependent class. **Internal tree-ordering conjecture.** $\mathscr C$ has a dependent internal tree-ordering expansion if and only if $\mathscr C$ has bounded twin-width. This would characterize bounded twin-width for hereditary weakly sparse graph classes through dependent internal tree-orderings; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
full_record.source_name: Hector Buffière, Yuquan Lin, Jaroslav Nešetřil, Patrice Ossona de Mendez and Sebastian Siebertz, “Characterizations of monadically dependent tree-ordered weakly sparse structures”, arXiv:2601.16039 (2026).
full_record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2025–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2505.00594](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00594).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.16039

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).

full_record.title: Sazdanovic–Scofield homological span conjecture for chromatic homology
full_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $v$ vertices and $b$ blocks, and let $\mathcal{A}_m$ be the algebra used to define its chromatic homology. Write $H_{*,*}^{\mathcal{A}_m}(G)$ for the resulting bigraded chromatic homology and let $hspan$ denote its homological span.

**Sazdanovic–Scofield conjecture.** The homological span satisfies

$$
hspan\left(H_{*,*}^{\mathcal{A}_m}(G)\right)=v-b.
$$

The paper states that it proves this conjecture using the spanning tree model, so the conjecture is resolved in the setting considered. The result gives a graph-theoretic description of the homological span of chromatic homology over $\mathcal{A}_m$.
full_record.source_name: Aninda Banerjee, Apratim Chakraborty, Swarup Kumar Das and Pravakar Paul, “A spanning tree model for chromatic homology”, arXiv:2504.00834 (2025).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00834

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of April 2025); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

full_record.title: The characterization of perpane graphs as perfect cancellation graphs
full_record.statement:
A graph is **perpane** if it admits the perpane property, and a **perfect cancellation graph** if it admits a perfect cancellation ordering.

**Perpane–perfect cancellation conjecture.** A graph is perpane if and only if it is a perfect cancellation graph.

The paper identifies this characterization as its main open problem. Resolving it requires a better understanding of perfect graphic parity networks, for which several open questions remain.
full_record.source_name: Yixin Cao, Yiren Lu, Junhong Nie, Xiaoming Sun and Guojing Tian, “Toward Minimum Graphic Parity Networks”, arXiv:2509.10070 (2025).
full_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.10070

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2025). “Thus, to answer the conjecture, we need to better understand perfect graphic parity networks, for which there are several open questions.”
